summary: Intermittent authz path resolution flapping for hybrid provisioning leading to STS token exchange failures
description: Issue summary: Over the last 36 hours several hybrid provisioning jobs (provisioner -> dedicated & private paths) have intermittently failed during STS token exchange: service-broker reports 'token exchange denied' or 'audience mismatch'. Impact: Provisioning jobs for Dedicated and Private onboards in us-east and eu-west are intermittently blocked; end-to-end deploys retry for several minutes and sometimes fall back to manual intervention. Business impact: delayed customer onboarding and increased oncall load. Scope: observed across multiple accounts and projects that cross-folder org-policy boundaries.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a provisioner job that uses cross-account STS token exchange (gcp->aws assume role) against a folder-scoped org-policy that recently had an audit-only policy change
Observe service-broker logs for token exchange attempt
Run 'aws sts assume-role' using the service account impersonation token produced by our token broker and note rejection with 'AccessDenied' or audience mismatch
logs: 2026-03-11T02:14:22Z service-broker ERROR token_exchange: denied (audience mismatch) account=acme-prod request_id=4f7a...
2026-03-11T02:14:22Z scheduler WARN retrying job provisioner-usr-137 attempt=3 exit_code=1
gcloud: IAMPolicyBinding check returned 'DENY' for resource //cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/folders/12345 due to orgpolicy constraint 'restrictServiceAccountImpersonation'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Recent org-policy change at folder level introduced a condition on serviceAccount impersonation tags; broker tokens don't surface expected session tags leading to policy deny
Hypothesis B: Token exchange audience claim truncated when broker proxies between GCP and AWS due to header encoding change in service-broker v1.8.0
Observed correlation: failures spike when provisioning is routed through eu-west broker-facing instances running v1.8.0; staging instances on v1.7.9 unaffected
Ran policy-simulator for folder 12345 and reproduced DENY when session tag 'team' is missing
Found a codepath in service-broker where tag propagation is skipped for ephemeral tokens created via the 'bridge' flow (file: broker/token_bridge.go:line ~240)
Temporary workaround: set fallback role mapping on the provisioner to use project-scoped role (less strict) — applied to two affected tenants while we investigate
current_workaround: Applied fallback project-scoped role mapping for two stuck onboarding jobs; increased broker instance count in eu-west to reduce queuing; oncall running manual retries where automatic retries exhausted.
action_items: Short-term: Roll back service-broker change (v1.8.0) in eu-west to v1.7.9 for broker-facing instances (assigned: Ethan)
Short-term: Add explicit session tag propagation in token_bridge.go and ship hotfix PR to infra (assigned: SRE team)
Medium-term: Run org-policy simulation across all folders to detect mismatch conditions and publish inventory (assigned: Security Ops)
Medium-term: Add CI regression test for session tag propagation covering bridge flow (assigned: Developer Experience)
resolution: (pending) Hotfix PR applied to service-broker to ensure session tag propagation for bridge flow; rolling deploy scheduled 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC. After deploy we will monitor for 48 hours and confirm no further STS denials. Final resolution will include an org-policy inventory and automated policy-simulation gate in provisioning pipeline.
